title: Enriched Hom identifies the twisted-arrow coupling
statement:
Use locally Kan simplicial categories and their coherent nerve as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], spaces and internal functor simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the twisted-arrow coupling of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a simplicial category in sufficiently large fixed universes, with all mapping simplicial sets Kan. Let $\operatorname{Kan}$ be the simplicial category of Kan complexes with internal functor simplicial sets as mapping objects, and put $\mathcal S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan})$ and $C=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A)$. The opposite simplicial category has $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}(a,b)=\mathcal A(b,a)$ with reversed composition; a product of simplicial categories has pairs of objects and products of mapping complexes. The enriched Hom functor
$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A\longrightarrow\operatorname{Kan},\qquad(a,b)\longmapsto\mathcal A(a,b),$$
acts on mapping complexes by precomposition in the first variable and postcomposition in the second. Write $H:C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C\to\mathcal S$ for its coherent nerve, using the nerve identifications for products and opposites. Put
$$W=\{\Delta^0\}\times_{\mathcal S,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal S),\qquad r=\operatorname{ev}_1:W\to\mathcal S.$$
There is an equivalence over $C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$ between $\operatorname{Tw}(C)$ and $(C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C)\times_{H,\mathcal S,r}W$. On a vertex represented by an edge $a\to b$, comparison with the fiber $\mathcal A(a,b)$ is the coherent-nerve mapping comparison. It carries the identity edge to the enriched identity point with its unit homotopy. The equivalence is natural for simplicial functors and respects the simplicial precomposition and postcomposition maps, including their higher composition and unit homotopies.

source.place: Kerodon Construction 8.3.6.1 (03N6), Proposition 8.3.6.2 (03N7), and Definition 8.3.5.1 (03MT) spelling out Hom-functor as transport for the twisted-arrow coupling; Proposition 8.3.5.5 (03NK) identifies the identity witness. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Write $B=C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$. For mapping simplices $u:a'\to a$, $z:a\to b$, $v:b\to b'$, the formula $(u,z,v)\mapsto vzu$ is simplicial. Associativity gives $(v'v)z(uu')=v'(vzu)u'$ and the enriched identities give its two unit equations. By the internal-Hom adjunction this defines the enriched Hom functor. The coherent nerve preserves products directly from its definition as enriched functors out of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$. Reversing vertex labels in the subset-poset formula identifies its opposite with the nerve of the opposite enriched category. Thus its nerve is precisely the stated $H:B\to\mathcal S$. For Kan complexes $X,Y$, the map $Y\to\Delta^0$ lifts every horn, hence is a right fibration. Taking base $\Delta^0$ in the mapping-complex clause of the simplicial-right-fibration presentation shows that $\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)$ is Kan. Thus $\operatorname{Kan}$ is locally Kan, and both $C$ and $\mathcal S$ are quasicategories by the locally Kan clause of the coherent-nerve node.

source.place: Construction 8.3.6.1 (03N6); enriched composition and coherent-nerve subset-poset definitions.

proof.text: Construct a map $t:\operatorname{Tw}(C)\to\mathcal S_{\Delta^0/}$ over $H$, where $\mathcal S_{\Delta^0/}$ is the join coslice with initial vertex $\Delta^0$. An $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Tw}(C)$ is an enriched functor $f:\mathfrak C[N(\overline{[n]}\star[n])]\to\mathcal A$. Its image under $H\lambda$ is the enriched diagram $F(j)=\mathcal A(f(\bar j),f(j))$. Adjoin a first object $*$ to $[n]$ and extend this diagram by $\widetilde F(*)=\Delta^0$. The mapping set $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}](*,j)$ is the nerve of the inclusion poset of nonempty subsets $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,j\}$ with maximum $j$ (the full subset is $\{*\}\cup I$). Define its map to $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,F(j))=F(j)$ by applying $f$ to the subset $\bar I\cup I$ of $\overline{[n]}\star[n]$. On all mapping sets between the old objects use $F$. The following step verifies that these data define an enriched functor; its coherent nerve is the desired simplex of the coslice.

source.place: Construction 8.3.6.5 (03NA), rewritten with the inclusion-poset coherent-nerve convention of the existing node.

proof.text: Here is the composition and operator check for Step 2. A mapping simplex from $i$ to $j$ is a chain of subsets $T\subseteq\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing $i,j$; $F$ acts on $z$ by $f(T)\,z\,f(\bar T)$. Composing it with a subset $I$ having maximum $i$ replaces $I$ by $I\cup T$. Since $\overline{I\cup T}\cup(I\cup T)=\bar T\cup\bar I\cup I\cup T$, and composition in $\mathfrak C$ is union, applying $f$ gives exactly $f(T)f(\bar I\cup I)f(\bar T)$. This holds pointwise on chains of subsets, hence on the whole mapping simplicial set. Composition among old objects holds because $F$ is the enriched Hom diagram; identities correspond to singleton subsets. For an arbitrary monotone $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, images of subsets satisfy $\overline{\theta(I)}\cup\theta(I)=(\bar\theta\star\theta)(\bar I\cup I)$. This also holds for noninjective $\theta$, so both faces and degeneracies commute. These equations prove enriched functoriality and the required simplicial map $t$, with the exact projection equation $Ut=H\lambda$.

source.place: Exercise 8.3.6.6 (03NC): explicit union and monotone-image calculation, rather than invoking the exercise without its argument.

proof.text: There is a comparison $d:\mathcal S_{\Delta^0/}\to W$ over $\mathcal S$: on an $n$-simplex $h:\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to\mathcal S$, precompose with the monotone map $[n]\times[1]\to[0]\star[n]$ sending $(j,0)$ to the new first vertex and $(j,1)$ to $j$. Interchange the product factors to match the internal functor convention. This is exactly the opposite-category dual of the map $\delta_y$ of the slice-arrow-equivalence node, applied to $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $y=\Delta^0$; reversing labels sends its final-vertex equation to our initial-vertex equation. That node therefore makes $d$ an equivalence over $\mathcal S$. The coslice projection is a left fibration by the opposite of the slice-right-fibration node, and $W\to\mathcal S$ is a left fibration by the universal-left-fibration node. Apply the right-fibration fiber node to their opposites: $d$ induces homotopy equivalences on vertex fibers. Reversing a simplicial homotopy reverses the parameter interval, so taking opposites preserves homotopy equivalences. The composite $(\lambda,dt)$ defines the actual simplicial map $\Phi:\operatorname{Tw}(C)\to B\times_{H,\mathcal S,r}W$ over $B$.

source.place: Construction 8.3.6.5 and Proposition 8.3.6.7 (03ND), with the join-coslice to fixed-source arrow comparison supplied by the existing slice-arrow node.

proof.text: Fix $a,b$ and put $K=\mathcal A(a,b)$. Let $M_C^L(a,b)$ have $n$-simplices $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to C$ with first vertex $a$ and entire last face constant at $b$. Equivalently $M_C^L(a,b)=\operatorname{Map}_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}(b,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$, by reversing labels. The source-fixed slice comparison in the twisted-arrow node is a map of left fibrations over $C$. Taking opposites and applying the right-fibration fiber node shows that its restriction $\iota:M_C^L(a,b)\to\operatorname{Tw}(C)_{(a,b)}$ is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. The source coslice projection is a left fibration by the opposite slice-right-fibration statement. This establishes the actual fiber comparison, including empty fibers, without identifying right- and left-pinched mapping sets.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.6.7 (03ND), using Corollary 8.1.2.11 (03K1); its hypotheses are supplied by the existing source-fixed slice and right-fibration fiber statements.

proof.text: On these fibers the composite $t_{a,b}\iota$ is a canonical isomorphism $M_C^L(a,b)\cong M_{\mathcal S}^L(\Delta^0,K)$. We spell out the dependence on $K$ that proves this, rather than inferring coherence from equivalence of homotopy types. Collapse the final face of $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n$ to $b$ and call the resulting two-vertex simplicial set $J_L^n$. Its coherent realization is obtained by the simplex-colimit formula in the coherent-nerve node. By the adjunction, $\mathfrak C[J_L^n]=\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]}\mathfrak C[\Delta^0]$, with the second map collapsing the final face. This has two formal objects, identity endomorphism complexes and no mapping simplices from the final object to the first: no composable path can return to an earlier vertex. Thus an enriched functor with the two object images fixed at $a,b$ is exactly a simplicial map $Q_L^n=\mathfrak C[J_L^n](a,b)\to K$. This is the left-hand version of the pinched construction $J^n,Q^n$ in the pinched-resolution node, obtained by reversing ordered labels. An enriched functor from this same two-object realization to $\operatorname{Kan}$, with object images $\Delta^0,K$, is instead exactly a simplicial map into $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,K)=K$, so in each degree both sides are the same set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q_L^n,K)$, with the same operators. Under the coslice inclusion, the barred block of a subset $\bar I\cup I$ collapses to $a$ and the unbarred block remains $I$; hence Step 2's formula becomes the same map on $Q_L^n$. Thus $t_{a,b}\iota$ is this isomorphism, naturally in $a,b$ and in enriched functors.

source.place: Remark 4.6.7.17 (03LK) and the subset calculation in the proof of Proposition 8.3.6.7; the argument is included from the coherent-realization and pinched definitions.

proof.text: Since $\iota$ and $t_{a,b}\iota$ are homotopy equivalences, $t_{a,b}$ is one as well: put $g=t_{a,b}\iota$, choose homotopy inverses $u$ to $g$ and $j$ to $\iota$, and set $s=\iota u$. Then $t_{a,b}s=gu\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $st_{a,b}\simeq st_{a,b}\iota j=\iota u g j\simeq\iota j\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Step 4 gives the same property for the fiber of $d$, so $\Phi$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on each vertex fiber. Its source is a left fibration by the twisted-arrow node, and its target is a left fibration: it is the pullback of $r$, and a horn lifting problem in the pullback is a horn lifting problem for $r$ with its fixed base coordinate. The last clause of the simplicial-right-fibration presentation now gives an inverse to $\Phi$ up to simplicial homotopies over $B$. This is the required equivalence over $C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$. The fiber comparison just computed is induced by the coherent-nerve adjunction, so its identification with $K$ is precisely the coherent-nerve mapping comparison, retaining the vertex-to-edge convention.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.6.7 (03ND), proof by the actual maps on vertex fibers and the left-fibration fiberwise criterion.

proof.text: For $n=0$, the subset formula sends the edge $z:a\to b$ to the point $z\in\mathcal A(a,b)$, and in particular sends the identity to the enriched identity. For a simplicial functor $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$, applying $G$ after $f(\bar I\cup I)$ is equal to the same formula for $Gf$, proving naturality of the whole map, not merely of its fibers. Precomposition and postcomposition are $z\mapsto vzu$; the union equation in Step 3 proves compatibility on all mapping simplices. The two unit equations and associativity for enriched composition are preserved on every chain of subsets, and face restrictions give their coherence equations in every dimension. Consequently their coherent-nerve images supply the unit homotopy and the higher composition homotopies in the assertion. The map $d$ is defined by a fixed monotone map and commutes with all these restrictions, so the same clauses hold for $\Phi$.

source.place: Construction 8.3.6.5 (03NA), Exercise 8.3.6.6 (03NC), and the identity normalization of Proposition 8.3.5.5 (03NK).

proof_origin.place: Online subsection 8.3.6, Construction 8.3.6.5 (03NA), Exercise 8.3.6.6 (03NC), and proof of Proposition 8.3.6.7 (03ND), with Remark 4.6.7.17 (03LK). Not archived in literature/; expanded in the inclusion-poset convention of the existing coherent-nerve node.
